items.prompt: Which word is a modal verb? You should bring a hat tomorrow.

options.why: Bring is the main verb. It tells us the action.
Hat is a noun.
Tomorrow tells us when.

hints: A modal verb comes before the main verb.
Modal verbs include words such as can, might and must.
Find the main verb, bring. Which word comes just before it?
items.explanation: Should is a modal verb. It comes before the main verb bring and shows that this is good advice.

items.prompt: Which modal verb shows that something is certain?

options.why: Might shows that something is possible but not certain.
Could shows a possibility.
May shows a possibility, or asks for permission.

hints: Some modal verbs show possibility and some show certainty.
Put each word into the sentence: It ___ rain tomorrow. Which sounds most sure?
Cross out the words that mean perhaps.
items.explanation: Will shows that the speaker is sure something is going to happen. Might, could and may only show that it is possible.

items.prompt: Put the sentences in order from least likely to most likely.
items: We will not go to the beach.
We might go to the beach.
We will probably go to the beach.
We will definitely go to the beach.
hints: Look at the words that show how sure the speaker is.
Find the sentence that says it will not happen, and the one that is completely sure.
Start with the sentence that has not in it.
items.explanation: Will not means no chance, might means possible, will probably means likely and will definitely means certain.

items.prompt: Choose the best modal verb. You ___ wear a helmet when you ride a motorbike. It is the law.

options.why: Might suggests it is only a possibility, but a law is a rule.
Could suggests a choice, but a law must be followed.
Would is used for things that depend on something else, or for polite requests.

hints: The second sentence is a clue.
A law is a rule that everyone has to follow.
Look for the modal verb that means it is necessary.
items.explanation: Must shows that something is necessary or a rule. Wearing a helmet is the law, so you must wear one.

items.prompt: Make the sentence less certain. Write one modal verb. The bus ___ be late.
hints: The sentence should show that you are not sure.
Choose a modal verb that means perhaps.
Try saying: The bus ___ be late, but I am not sure.
items.explanation: Might, may and could all show that something is possible but not certain.

items.prompt: Match each sentence to what the modal verb shows.
pairs: You must stop at a red light.
You are able to do it.
It might be windy at the beach.
hints: Each modal verb has a different job.
Think about whether the sentence is a rule, advice, ability, permission or possibility.
Start with must. Is a red light a rule or advice?
items.explanation: Must shows a rule, should gives advice, can shows ability, may gives permission and might shows possibility.

items.prompt: Which sentence gives advice rather than an order?

options.text: You should check your answers before you hand in your test.
You must hand in your test at ten o’clock.
options.why: Must makes this a rule, so it is an order.
This is a command. It tells you what to do.

options.text: You will hand in your test now.
options.why: Will makes this sound like an instruction you cannot refuse.

hints: Advice is a suggestion about what would be a good idea.
Look for the modal verb that suggests a good idea, not a rule.
Find the sentence that a kind friend might say to help you.
items.explanation: Should gives advice: it suggests a good idea. Must, will and a command all tell you that you have to do something.

items.prompt: Choose 2 sentences that show possibility.

options.why: Must shows that it is necessary.
This tells us something that definitely happened.

options.text: Ayu will join the choir on Monday.
options.why: Will shows that the speaker is certain.

hints: Possibility means something could happen, but we are not sure.
Look for modal verbs or adverbs such as might, may, perhaps and maybe.
Cross out any sentence that sounds certain or is a rule.
items.explanation: Might and perhaps both show that something is possible but not certain.

items.prompt: The lights are off and the car has gone. Which modal verb shows you are sure? They ___ be out.

options.why: Can’t be out means it is impossible that they are out, but the clues show the opposite.
Should is mainly used for advice or for what we expect.
Shall is used for offers and suggestions, like Shall we go?

hints: The first sentence gives you clues.
When clues make us sure something is true, we use a modal verb for a strong guess.
Ask: are the clues weak or strong? How sure can you be?
items.explanation: Must can show that we are sure something is true because of the evidence. The lights are off and the car has gone, so they must be out.

items.prompt: Rina was at school all day, so it is impossible that she ate the cake. Which sentence means the same?

options.why: Mustn’t is a rule telling her not to eat it.

options.text: Rina might have eaten the cake.
options.why: Might have shows it is possible, but we know it is not.

options.text: Rina should have eaten the cake.
options.why: Should have suggests that it was expected, which is not the meaning.

options.text: Rina can’t have eaten the cake.

hints: The first sentence shows that something is impossible.
Look for the modal phrase that means it is impossible that something happened.
Think about the opposite of must have. What do we say when something definitely did not happen?
items.explanation: Can’t have shows that we are sure something did not happen. Rina was at school, so she can’t have eaten the cake.

items.prompt: Dewi ___ swim when she was five.
hints: The sentence is about ability in the past.
Could is the past of can.
Check which word shows ability.
items.explanation: Could shows ability in the past.

items.prompt: Which sentence shows ability?

options.why: Must shows obligation.
Might shows possibility.
Should shows advice.

hints: Ability means being able to do something.
Can often shows ability.
Choose the sentence about what Yuki is able to do.
items.explanation: Can shows ability.

items.prompt: Build the sentence.
hints: Start with You.
The modal verb comes before the main verb.
More water goes last.
items.explanation: Should shows advice.

items.prompt: Write a modal verb that asks politely. ___ I borrow your ruler, please?
hints: Think of polite questions.
May and could are polite.
Choose a modal verb for asking permission.
items.explanation: May, can and could all ask permission.

items.prompt: Which sentence uses a modal verb correctly?

options.why: Do not use to after can.
Modal verbs do not take s.
The main verb stays in its base form.

hints: A modal verb is followed by the base form.
Modal verbs never add s.
Do not add to after can.
items.explanation: A modal verb is followed by the base form of the main verb.

items.prompt: Sort the sentences by meaning.

items.text: It must be Leo at the door.
We could go to the beach.
You must keep quiet in the library.

hints: Think what the modal verb tells us.
Must can show a rule or being sure.
Might and could show possibility.
items.explanation: Modal verbs show obligation, certainty or possibility.

items.prompt: Match each modal verb to the degree of certainty.
hints: Think about how sure each word sounds.
Might is the weakest.
Will is the strongest.
items.explanation: Might is a small chance, should is probable, must is almost certain and will is certain.

items.prompt: Bayu is not sure where his keys are. He ___ have left them at school.

options.why: Must shows he is sure.
Will shows certainty about the future.
Should shows advice.

hints: Bayu is guessing.
Choose a word that shows possibility.
He does not know for sure.
items.explanation: Might shows possibility.

items.prompt: The name Dewi is on the bag. It is almost certainly hers. It ___ be Dewi’s bag.
hints: The speaker is very sure.
Choose a strong modal verb.
Might is too weak.
items.explanation: Must shows strong certainty.

items.prompt: Visitors ___ not touch the paintings. If you are tired, you ___ sit on the benches.
hints: One is a rule and one is permission.
Must is strong.
May gives permission.
items.explanation: Must shows a rule and may gives permission.

items.prompt: Complete the table.
head: Modal verb
Shows
Example
hints: Read the example.
Possibility means maybe.
Should gives advice.
items.explanation: May shows possibility and should gives advice.

items.prompt: Choose all the sentences where the modal verb shows advice.

options.text: You should rest if you feel dizzy.
You must show your ticket at the gate.
options.why: Must here is a rule.

options.text: It might be a long wait.
options.why: Might shows possibility.

options.text: If I were you, I would ask a teacher.

options.why: Can shows ability.

hints: Advice tells someone what is a good idea.
Should, ought to and would can give advice.
A rule is not advice.
items.explanation: Should, ought to and would give advice.

items.prompt: Which sentence means it is NOT necessary?

options.why: Mustn’t means forbidden.

options.text: You don’t have to bring lunch.

options.why: Can’t means not allowed.
Shouldn’t is advice not to.

hints: Not necessary means you can choose.
Mustn’t is a ban.
Look for have to.
items.explanation: Don’t have to means there is no need.

items.prompt: Which sentence shows the LEAST certainty?

options.why: Must have shows strong belief.
Should have shows expectation.
Will have shows certainty.

hints: Compare how sure each sentence is.
Could shows possibility.
Choose the weakest.
items.explanation: Could have shows only a possibility.
